# Owners, terminals, closing and returning

John accepted this model on 23 November 2026 (strategy: `/cosmoshot/store/taskboard/owners-and-terminals-strategy-20261123.md`).

## The rule

1. **One owner, one agent key, one working folder, one named primary terminal.** That is the normal state. Other teams ask the
   owner, never a session: the owner key is the name.
2. **A harness swap is the same owner.** When tokens run out on one lane, the work moves from a Claude terminal to a Codex one (or back):
   one registry line changes (`harness`), nothing is renamed, no successor name is made up.
3. **A second live terminal of one owner is abnormal.** It shows a calm warning, not an error. Mail goes to whichever session acts
   first, so nobody knows which one answers. A helper session may exist only if its first line says it is a helper, and it does not
   answer the owner's mail.
4. **Parallel work is done with executors** (`cosmo-run executor`: no inbox, they hand back a file), not with a second session.
5. Many owners over the years is fine and most will be closed. A closed owner keeps its mark and its history and leaves the
   pickers. A retired key is never reused for another owner.

## Which memory store an owner writes (owner key and store key differ)

Memory finds the store from the working folder, by the longest folder prefix in `/cosmoshot/tools/projects.json`; the owner key
is only the board and message name. Check any folder with `cosmo-mem attachments --cwd FOLDER`.

| Owner (board key) | Its folder | Store project (`--project`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| platform | `/cosmoshot/platform` | platform |
| plc | `/cosmoshot/privatelocalchat`, `model-runtime` | plc |
| sonalon | `/cosmoshot/sonalon` | sonalon |
| cosmogenitor | `/cosmoshot/cosmogenitor` | cosmogenitor |
| cyberplanetary | `/cosmoshot/cyberplanetary*` | cyberplanetary |
| memory, infra, devops, taskboard, brand, aiofourown, business, concepts, lipsync, media_prod, ui_team, simulator | any other folder under `/cosmoshot` | program |

So an owner without a store of its own writes to `program` (which today is read-write on all six stores), and its
`what-this-project-is` and `handover` notes are named by the owner: `brand-handover`, `lipsync-what-this-project-is`, so they do not
collide with another owner's notes in the same store. An owner with its own store names them `handover` and `what-this-project-is`.

## Handing an owner to another harness (Claude to Codex or back): the process

Same owner, same key, same folder; only the terminal changes. **The outgoing agent writes the handover; it knows what matters.**
Memory keeps this process and the template; devops starts the terminal; John says when. A new session knows only what it is given:
a Codex agent unused for days has stale rules, so it starts **fresh** (not `resume`) unless it ran in the last day.

| Step | Who | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Say go | John | Names the owner and the incoming harness. Until step 7 the outgoing agent stays the primary. |
| 2 Drain | outgoing | Finish or park in-flight work: commit and push, end executors and watchers. Leave NOTHING in progress on the board: split each task in work (the finished part as its own done task linked as a dependency, the remainder not started); add, merge, edit or drop tasks as the work really is (see `board`). The gate fails while any task is in progress. |
| 3 Write the pack | outgoing | ONE handover note, template below: the memory note `handover` (`OWNER-handover` in `program`) and, if long, a repo file it points to. Refresh it; never pile up dated copies. |
| 4 Start the terminal | devops | Checklist below. Registry `harness` set to the new one; the new terminal is a helper until step 7. |
| 5 Read | incoming | `AGENTS.md` (comes with the folder), the pack, the owner's board tasks, waiting mail, `cosmo-mem read STORE _index.md`. |
| 6 Read-back | incoming, then outgoing | Incoming posts a board note: what it understood, what it will do first, questions. Outgoing answers on the same note. |
| 7 Cut over | John | Primary flag moves. Outgoing stops answering mail and closes its terminal. Never two primaries. |

**Template of the pack** (plain statements, no transcript, no secrets): (1) what the owner is for, its folders and repositories;
(2) board: every open task with its real one-line state and what to do first; (3) in flight: branches, worktrees, uncommitted files,
running processes, who else is involved; (4) decisions already taken, by whom, and the traps (what looks right and is not);
(5) mail and people: who waits for what, open threads; (6) what changed in the programme since the incoming agent last ran
(rules, tools, owners: point at memory notes and skills); (7) what not to do without asking John; (8) the first hour.

**Test of a good pack:** the incoming agent can say, without asking, what the three most urgent tasks are and why, what it must
not touch, and who is waiting on it. If not, the pack is incomplete: the outgoing agent adds to it.

**Starting a Codex terminal (devops):** the folder is trusted in `~/.codex/config.toml`; `.codex/config.toml` has the token-env block
(`COSMO_TEAM`); the hooks in `~/.codex/hooks.json` are trusted; Codex quota is not exhausted; skip the self-update prompt; the pane is in
the registered tmux session; `cosmo-msg waiting --to TEAM` is read once. Codex has no `SendMessage` and no background key: mail
reaches an idle Codex pane by a typed wake line, a busy one at its next hook.

## Closing an owner (Brand's checklist)

Do each item, then say on the board what was done. Nothing is deleted.

- [ ] **Owner entry and mark:** the owner stays in the board's owner table and the registry (`ops/agents.json`) with its mark; it is
      marked closed so it leaves the pickers ("Show closed" still lists it). Taskboard and devops make that change on a board task.
- [ ] **Memory store:** a `what-this-project-is` note that says what the owner was for and why it is closed, and a `handover`
      note as above. Index both. A closed owner without its own store leaves its notes in the store its folder maps to.
- [ ] **Working folder:** kept as it is, committed and pushed; no scratch left that the repository needs.
- [ ] **Honest statuses:** every task of the owner is `done`, `dropped` (with a note saying why), or handed to a named owner in
      a note. Never leave "in progress" on closed work.
- [ ] **Private stores:** a pointer (path or name, never contents) to any private store, and who may open it.
- [ ] **Inbox history:** the owner's `cosmo-msg` inbox is kept; mail still waiting is answered or moved by hand to the owner that
      now holds the work.
- [ ] **No secrets:** none in the store, the notes, the registry or the hand-over. A token the owner held is retired by its issuer.

## Starting a returning owner

1. Reopen the owner entry (registry and board) with the same key and the same mark. Do not make a new key.
2. Read the store: `what-this-project-is`, `handover`, and the board tasks still open.
3. Give it its working folder and **one** named primary terminal; set `harness` to the lane it starts on.
4. Check: `cosmo-msg teams` maps the folder to the owner; `cosmo-mem attachments --cwd FOLDER` shows its store;
   `cosmo-board team` names it; `cosmo-mem verify` is clean.
5. The first note it writes on the board says it has returned and what it will do first.

## What is enforced and what is a rule

Today the one-primary rule and the helper rule are rules. The registry check that refuses two agents on one working folder, and the
Desk warning for a second terminal, are board tasks under objective 189; when they land they enforce rules 1 and 3. Memory itself
is safe with two live sessions (every write passes the sha it read, the repository lock and one commit per change protect it); what
goes wrong is two sessions answering differently, not a corrupted store.
